parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files cover one concern: the Express HTTP adapter. RequestReader.ts parses and validates untyped request input, and it signals bad input with BadRequestError. createApp.ts wires up the routes and middleware. errorHandler.ts converts thrown errors into HTTP responses. The status-code mapping lives only in errorHandler.statusFor, which handles domain errors and BadRequestError. The input-validation rules ("is required", "must be a string") live only in RequestReader. Nothing goes around the module's own abstractions: errorHandler uses the BadRequestError exported by RequestReader instead of defining its own copy. One minor point: createApp builds its 404 'Route not found' response inline. It does not go through errorHandler, though it uses the same { error } response shape. This is a typical Express fallback route and does not duplicate any rule or invariant enough to count as a violation.
